raw_answer_text:
A1: The clock signal toggles at a constant, regular rate throughout the diagram.
A2: All three signals (request, acknowledge, completion) rest at low at the start.
A3: The request signal transitions (asserts) first.
A4: No, the acknowledge cannot assert before the request, since it is generated in response to the request being recognized.
A5: The request signal returns low once the acknowledge signal has asserted, indicating the receiver has recognized/accepted the request.
A6: The acknowledge signal returns low once it observes that the request signal has returned low (completing the four-phase handshake).
A7: The completion signal indicates that the requested operation/transfer has finished; it occurs after the request has been acknowledged, marking the end of the active data-transfer phase before the lines return to idle.
A8: (1) Request asserts high, (2) Acknowledge asserts high in response, (3) Request deasserts (returns low), (4) Acknowledge deasserts (returns low), completing the cycle.
